answer: Latency decay pricing. Each new identity pays an entry price that decays with the age of the oldest identity it references for routing; fresh clusters pay full price, older anchors discount it. Attackers mass-producing identities hit the jetty of a flat high price with no discounts, since their references are new. Honest agents inherit umber discounts from long-lived anchors, cutting their cost sharply. The river of renewals requires periodic re-registration priced by cluster age, so a sybil farm pays recurring full-rate fees per identity, scaling cost linearly with fleet size instead of once.
